project.description: Silversea (TingTing) is a Vietnamese trucking & container logistics platform: an Express 5 + Drizzle/Postgres backend, a React/Vite frontend, and a shared package for Zod contracts, navigation, and financial calculations. tour.title: Agent Contract & Dev Context
tour.description: Start with AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md — these define the closed-loop SDLC, mandatory QA gates, authority order, and progressive context-loading protocol that every coding agent must follow in this repo. They are the rulebook before any code.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: backend/src/index.ts boots Express, wires JWT auth + Casbin RBAC + audit middleware, mounts every route module, initializes notification/audit services, and starts the cron scheduler. It gives the bird's-eye view of the runtime: one process, many mounted routers, background jobs on a timer.
tour.languageLesson: Express 5 apps mount routers with app.use(mountPath, router). The order matters: middleware registered before routers runs for every request; the global error handler must be registered last.

tour.title: The Data Model
tour.description: backend/src/db/schema.ts is the single source of truth for the database — every table (trips, ledger, billing_documents, drivers, customers…), pgEnum, pgvector column, index, and check constraint lives here. The db client (db/index.ts) exports the connection pool and runs migrations on boot. Understanding this file unlocks every service that follows.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle ORM maps Postgres tables to typed TS objects via pgTable. pgvector columns use a customType since Drizzle has no native vector support; queries use the raw `<=>` operator through db.execute(sql`...`).

tour.title: Shared Contracts & Calculations
tour.description: The @tingting/shared package (shared/src/index.ts) is the monorepo's contract spine: Zod schemas validate every API request/response, while the calculations/ folder holds the money-math authorities (round2dp, trip totals, FIFO aging, salary, ISO 6346) used by both frontend and backend. Financial precision is centralized here, never duplicated.

tour.title: Auth & RBAC
tour.description: Every API route is gated. The auth middleware validates JWTs and loads the session user; the Casbin middleware enforces role/permission policies from casbin/policy.csv against model.conf. Roles (ADMIN, MANAGER, ACCOUNTANT, DRIVER, FORWARDER, CUSTOMER, CLERK) drive what each user can see and do.

tour.title: Trip Operations Routes
tour.description: routes/trips.ts is the largest route module: it mounts the trip lifecycle endpoints (create, dispatch, in-transit, complete, lock, cancel) and delegates to the trip services. It imports ~25 services and shared helpers, making it a hub for understanding how a trip flows through the system.

tour.title: Financial & Governance APIs
tour.description: routes/financial/index.ts aggregates the finance sub-routers — ledger, payments, penalties, advances, debt-offsets, billing-documents, governance-actions, credit-overrides, fuel-invoices, reports — each registering audit events. The governance-action queue is the authority gate: financial adjustments and credit overrides require MANAGER/DIRECTOR approval before they post.

tour.title: Business Services Core
tour.description: services/ holds the domain logic. Services like ledger.service.ts post transactions, billingDocument.service.ts assembles billing documents, advance.service.ts manages advance request/settlement state machines, and driver.service.ts + attendance.service.ts compute salary. These are where the business rules from the PRD live.

tour.title: Forwarder & Customer Portal
tour.description: The forwarder routes (routes/forwarder.ts) scope shipment and container operations to the forwarder role, while routes/portal/index.ts exposes the customer-facing API — shipments, statements, debit-note documents — scoped per-customer via business-unit links. This is the multi-tenant boundary.

tour.title: Background Jobs & Scheduler
tour.description: scheduler/index.ts registers cron-driven jobs: receivable reminders and retries, durable-effect processing, pending trip GPS capture, and salary-period processing. These keep the system's async work moving without manual intervention.

tour.title: AI Assistant
tour.description: The in-app AI assistant combines an LLM service layer (services/llm/), a tool registry (services/agent/tool.registry.ts), a WebSocket server (agentSocket.ts) for streaming, and a pgvector-backed FAQ fast-lane for grounded answers. It is a self-contained subsystem layered on top of the business services.

tour.title: Infrastructure & Deployment
tour.description: The stack runs as containers: the root Makefile and docker-compose.dev.yml orchestrate Postgres (:5441), Redis (:6391), the backend (:3001), frontend (:7174), and Adminer. Backend and frontend have their own multi-stage Dockerfiles; deploy/ holds production Nginx configs and a server provisioning script. This is how the app gets from source to a running system.
tour.languageLesson: Docker multi-stage builds separate the builder stage (with devDependencies for tsc) from the runtime stage (only production node_modules + dist), shrinking the final image and its attack surface.
